purpose: Guard the surprise-me contract and the subject-identifiability judgment: vague prompts get one scope question with 'Surprise me' as a real option; surprise-me runs dispatch without further subject questions (repo-grounded in a repo, substance-required outside one); short-but-identifiable subjects are never gated.
non_purpose: Not testing idea quality, critique rigor, or survivor counts — only the intake routing that decides whether and how agents dispatch.

grading_pipeline.stage_1: Programmatic transcript checks: did a scope question fire, did it include a surprise-me option, did dispatch proceed without subject questions, did the run end cleanly when substance was refused.
grading_pipeline.stage_2: LLM grader (grader.md) — judges question intent (subject-identifying vs subject-characterizing) and whether discovered subjects came from grounding material.

evals.name: vague-prompt-offers-surprise-me
evals.setup: CWD inside any real git repo.
evals.expected_behavior: Exactly one blocking scope question fires before any agent dispatch, offering: specify a subject, 'Surprise me' as a first-class option, and cancel. The run must not silently interpret 'improvements' as 'about this repo' and dispatch.
evals.must_not: Dispatching grounding/ideation agents without asking; asking about constraints, audience, tone, or success criteria (those are ce-brainstorm's questions).
evals.notes: Being inside a repo does not settle vagueness — the repo supplies grounding after a subject is settled, not the subject itself.

evals.name: surprise-me-in-repo-dispatches-clean
evals.prompt: /ce-ideate ideas -> user selects 'Surprise me' at the scope question
evals.setup: CWD inside a real git repo with substantive code.
evals.expected_behavior: After the surprise-me selection: zero further subject or characterization questions; run routes repo-grounded and dispatches grounding + ideation; the resulting ideas name concrete subjects discovered from repo material (files, subsystems, workflows), not generic software advice.
evals.must_not: A second question asking the user to narrow the focus; ideas untethered from the repo's actual content; skipping ideation because no subject was given.
evals.notes: Surprise-me is a first-class mode, not a fallback for users who can't name a subject.

evals.name: surprise-me-outside-repo-requires-substance
evals.prompt: /ce-ideate surprise me -> user gives a dismissive 'idk just go' when asked for material
evals.setup: CWD outside any git repo. User supplies no URL, description, draft, or paste.
evals.expected_behavior: One ask for substance (URL, description, or paste). When refused, the run states it needs material to proceed and ends cleanly for re-invocation — no agents dispatched.
evals.must_not: Dispatching ideation agents with no subject and no substance; looping on repeated asks.
evals.notes: 'Surprise me' outside a repo is only viable once there is something to surprise the user about.

evals.name: short-identifiable-subject-not-gated
evals.setup: CWD inside a git repo for a UI product (with or without existing dark-mode code).
evals.expected_behavior: No scope question — 'dark mode' plausibly names a specific subject. The run proceeds to mode classification and dispatch (a cheap repo footprint check is acceptable first).
evals.must_not: Firing the scope question on a short-but-identifiable phrase.
evals.notes: Vagueness is about what the words refer to, not phrase length — guards the judgment half of the gate. Run history (2026-07-26): evals 1-3 passed 3/3 each; eval 4 runs showed correct behavior 3/3 (zero questions, footprint check, dispatch notice reached) but were graded fail by a rubric line demanding observed dispatch while the runbook stopped runs at the dispatch decision — rubric corrected same day; adjudicated pass.
